permutationLabel: Late presentation (day 5) at a surgical follow-up clinic
summary: 52-year-old man at his post-hernia-repair review mentions a sudden worst-ever headache while lifting 5 days ago, now a milder persistent headache and neck ache.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Headache for five days since a sudden onset
inputs.hpi: At his post-operative hernia review he mentions that 5 days ago, while lifting a heavy box, he had a sudden severe headache, the worst of his life, that peaked within seconds; he lay down for 2 days. Now a milder persistent headache and aching neck. Took paracetamol. Did not seek help.

exam.neuro: GCS 15, no focal deficit, mild neck stiffness at extremes.
exam.abdomen: Right inguinal hernia repair wound healed.

surgicalHistory: Open right inguinal hernia repair 3 weeks ago

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected subarachnoid haemorrhage (sentinel headache, late presentation)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Thunderclap headache 5 days ago with persisting headache and neck ache: same-day referral for CT head and further investigation (CTA / LP) for SAH.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no node for this condition (surgical diseases only); top 3 inguinal hernia, cholecystitis, GORD. Symptom inference ranks SAH #2.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add medical-emergency diseases to lib/pane-engine (or a separate medical-mimic layer) driven by labs/vitals/chips, or show the symptom-inference leader beside the PANE top 3 when PANE has no matching node.

emergencyLevel.note: Five days on, still a same-day investigation: a sentinel bleed precedes a larger one.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web: Triage "priority_24_48h" (score 15). Instead, "Hernia — elective repair indicated" fires from the healed repair in the exam text.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Add neurological red-flag rules to lib/triage-engine rules.ts (sudden focal weakness/facial droop/speech disturbance, thunderclap headache, neck stiffness with fever/non-blanching rash, saddle anaesthesia with bladder/bowel change, new leg weakness with known cancer) → emergency.

mustAlarm.knownGapNote: Web: No SAH alarm; the only safety prompts are pre-op bloods and an elective hernia repair.
mustAlarm.proposedFix: Add neurological safety prompts to clinical-inference.ts keyed on symptoms/HPI text (FAST → CT head + stroke team; thunderclap → CT head ± LP/CTA + neurosurgery; meningism/purpura → blood cultures + IV ceftriaxone now; saddle anaesthesia/retention → emergency MRI + spinal team; cancer + back pain/weakness → MRI whole spine + dexamethasone + MSCC coordinator).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No CT head, CTA or LP.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add neurological safety prompts to clinical-inference.ts keyed on symptoms/HPI text (FAST → CT head + stroke team; thunderclap → CT head ± LP/CTA + neurosurgery; meningism/purpura → blood cultures + IV ceftriaxone now; saddle anaesthesia/retention → emergency MRI + spinal team; cancer + back pain/weakness → MRI whole spine + dexamethasone + MSCC coordinator).

guideline.name: NICE NG228 — Subarachnoid haemorrhage caused by a ruptured aneurysm: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Suspect SAH with thunderclap headache (sudden, severe, peaking within minutes); non-contrast CT head immediately; if CT is normal and done more than 6 h after onset, consider lumbar puncture at least 12 h after onset; if SAH confirmed: CT angiography and discussion with a neurosurgical centre; nimodipine
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Subarachnoid haemorrhage caused by a ruptured aneurysm: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG228. London: NICE; 2022.

rationale: A thunderclap headache days ago still needs investigation today (NICE NG228). The setting (surgical clinic, routine booking) tests whether the engines escalate.
